topic: Planting a garden with my father
title: Rows of Green
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Dad showed me how to make a row,
and how deep the seeds should go,
his hands were brown from April ground,
he hummed a tune without a sound.

[Chorus]
Rows of green, rows of green,
prettiest thing I've ever seen,
tomatoes climbing up the wooden fence that my father built the summer I turned nine,
rows of green, rows of green,
and every single evening we would water them together until the sun went down behind the line.

[Verse 2]
Now his hands are slower than before,
I carry water to the door,
he points at where the beans should be,
and leaves the digging up to me.

[Chorus]
Rows of green, rows of green,
prettiest thing I've ever seen,
tomatoes climbing up the wooden fence that my father built the summer I turned nine,
rows of green, rows of green,
and every single evening we would water them together until the sun went down behind the line.
reason: Chorus lines are 6-8 syllables except two that run past 20 syllables, breaking the melody in every chorus.
